forces.title: Structural Shift to Online Shopping Reshapes Retail Real Estate
forces.description: The ongoing structural shift towards online shopping, exacerbated by the emergence of agentic commerce, is fundamentally altering demand for retail real estate in the Netherlands. Investors are increasingly focusing on prime retail locations where vacancy risks are contained, leading to a concentration of capital in top-tier assets. This trend contributes to a decline in the overall retail real estate stock, necessitating adaptation for developers and owners.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Retailer Demand for Store Investment Drives Property Activity
forces.description: Irish grocery and convenience retailers are actively investing in new and revamped stores to attract and retain footfall, leading to robust funding activity for store purchases and renovation projects. This ongoing expansion and modernization by major brands like Tesco, Aldi, and Lidl acts as a significant tailwind for the Retail & Mixed-Use Development sector, ensuring continued demand for well-located and high-quality retail real estate.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Reinvigorated In-Store Retail Boosts Shopping Centre Investment
forces.description: A post-pandemic resurgence in in-store retail, coupled with the entry of new international brands into Ireland, is driving strong investor interest and transaction activity in retail parks and shopping centres. High occupancy levels (95%+) nationwide reflect healthy demand for physical retail spaces, providing a significant tailwind for developers and owners of these assets in the Retail & Mixed-Use Development sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: AI Integration Boosts Efficiency in Mixed-Use Property Development
forces.description: The adoption of AI in real estate development, particularly for mixed-use properties, is identified as a significant upside driver. AI applications such as construction site assistants and procurement optimization can lead to a 400-700 basis points margin uplift and a 30% compression in project timelines. This enhances operational efficiency and accelerates capital deployment cycles, offering a structural advantage for developers.
forces.source_title: The AI-First Real Estate Company: An Opportunity for Structural Advantage

forces.title: AI Reshapes Physical Store Role, Necessitating Strategic Real Estate Adaptation
forces.description: The growing use of AI for routine purchases is fundamentally altering the role of physical stores, leading to fewer but more valuable in-store visits. This structural shift compels landlords and developers of shopping centers and mixed-use properties to redefine store missions, focusing on either convenience or discovery. Strategic investment and operational changes are critical for physical retail assets to remain relevant and thrive in the future.
forces.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era

forces.title: Demand for "Third Places" Boosts Shopping Centers and Mixed-Use Environments
forces.description: Consumers across all age groups are increasingly seeking "third places" outside of home and work for social benefit and experiences. This growing demand directly supports shopping centers and mixed-use retail environments, which can position themselves as experiential destinations. This trend provides a tailwind for developers and landlords in the Retail & Mixed-Use Development sector, encouraging investment in creating engaging physical spaces beyond pure transactional retail.
forces.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era

forces.title: Capital Constraints Hinder Necessary Retail Real Estate Transformation
forces.description: Retailers and real estate developers, while aware of evolving consumer behaviors driven by AI, face significant capital constraints. This limits their ability to make the substantial, non-incremental changes required to adapt physical stores and shopping centers. Failure to invest sufficiently in redefining store missions and creating new experiences poses a key risk to the long-term relevance and profitability of retail real estate assets.
forces.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era

forces.title: Delay in AI Adoption Risks Growing Gap in Consumer Expectations
forces.description: Retail and mixed-use developers who delay the adoption of AI technologies risk creating a widening gap between evolving consumer expectations and the capabilities of their physical retail environments. As AI capabilities accelerate and reshape shopping behaviors, an incremental response will be insufficient, potentially leading to a struggle to meet modern demands and maintain relevance in the competitive real estate market.
forces.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era

forces.title: Younger Generations' Spending Power Drives New Retail Format Demand
forces.description: As millennials and Gen Z gain greater purchasing power, their distinct behaviors and preferences are poised to drive the next wave of retail change. These digitally native consumers prioritize experiential retail, frictionless payment, and omnichannel experiences, creating an upside opportunity for retail and mixed-use developers who can innovate and adapt their physical spaces to meet these evolving demands for engagement and convenience.
forces.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era

viewpoints.title: Online Shopping Shift Dampens Investor Demand for Retail Real Estate
viewpoints.description: The Dutch commercial real estate market sees investor demand for retail properties concentrating solely in prime locations due to the ongoing structural shift towards online shopping and the rise of agentic commerce. This trend limits vacancy risks in top-tier assets but contributes to a broader decline in overall retail real estate stock. This suggests a cautious outlook for non-prime retail developments and a focus on high-quality assets.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Robust Investment in Irish Grocery & Convenience Retail Store Development
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland reports robust funding activity for store purchases and revamp proposals in Q1 2026 within the Irish grocery and convenience retail sector. This investment is driven by retailers' need for differentiation and to attract footfall through new and revamped stores. Major brands like Tesco, Aldi, Lidl, Dunnes, Centra, and Spar are actively expanding their physical footprint nationwide.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Strong Investor Interest in Irish Retail Parks & Shopping Centres Post-Pandemic
viewpoints.description: Investor interest in retail parks and shopping centres across Ireland has been robust over the past year, evidenced by significant transactions in key cities. This resurgence is fueled by a post-pandemic reinvigoration of in-store retail, attracting new international brands and boosting occupancy levels to over 95% nationwide. This positive trend underscores confidence in physical retail real estate.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: AI Redefining Physical Stores, Demanding Strategic Adaptations from Landlords
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that accelerating AI adoption for routine purchases will change the role of physical stores, making visits less frequent but more valuable. Landlords and developers must strategically define the mission of each shopping center to align with evolving consumer needs for convenience or discovery. Investment decisions over the next 3-5 years are crucial for physical retail's future relevance, driven by these AI-shaped shifts.
viewpoints.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era

new_opportunities.description: AI applications like construction site assistants and procurement optimization can significantly improve profit margins (400–700 bps) for developers of mixed-use properties, by enhancing efficiency and reducing costs across the development lifecycle.

AI-first development companies can compress project timelines by about 30% and accelerate capital deployment cycles, gaining a structural advantage through faster project completion and market entry for mixed-use properties.

market_sizing.methodology: AI applications in real estate, particularly for development companies (DevCos) involved in mixed-use properties, are projected to achieve a 400–700 basis points margin uplift and compress project timelines by approximately 30%. This value creation is driven by construction site assistants and procurement optimization, accelerating capital deployment.
market_sizing.source_title: The AI-First Real Estate Company: An Opportunity for Structural Advantage

new_opportunities.description: Landlords and developers can create high-value, discovery-oriented retail destinations by integrating retail, dining, and experiences that are not replicable online. This strategy earns more of consumers' time and caters to the demand for "third places," enhancing property value and appeal.

For convenience-focused consumers, landlords must prioritize speed, easy access, seamless pickups/returns, and the ability to complete multiple shopping missions efficiently within a single property. This enhances customer satisfaction and footfall for essential retail services.

Landlords can leverage consumer behavior data and predictive analytics to curate optimal retail ecosystems, ensuring the tenant mix aligns with shopper missions and maximizes collective performance. This strategic approach enhances property relevance and profitability.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of evolving consumer behavior in an AI-shaped retail marketplace indicates significant opportunities for landlords and developers who adapt their properties to serve distinct shopping missions. This involves becoming "placemakers" for discovery-oriented retail and optimizing for convenience, leveraging data-backed decisions.
market_sizing.source_title: Shopping in the age of AI: Redefining stores for a new era
